events.description: Hadestown, previously scheduled for March 16, 2026, at the DECC Symphony Hall, has been POSTPONED due to travel conditions and restrictions surrounding the Midwest Winter Storm. The performance has been rescheduled for Monday, October 19, 2026. All current tickets will be valid for the October performance. COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: Introduction to 3D Modeling and Printing: From Idea to Object, with Tim Lutgen
events.address: 5503 W. Range View Drive, Hurley, WI
events.description: Have you ever looked at a broken piece of plastic, had a missing part for a project, or had a creative idea in your head and wished you could simply print the solution? “Introduction to 3D Modeling and Printing: From Idea to Object” with Tim Lutgen is the perfect place to turn those digital concepts into physical reality! Slated for three afternoons in a row, from 4 to 6 p.m. on Oct. 19-21, at Hurley High School, this course is designed for adults who are curious about the “how-to” behind 3D printing. Tim will demystify the process by breaking it down into two core components: designing, using CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software, and printing, learning how to “slice” your model and operate a 3D printer to bring it to life. No prior engineering experience is needed, just a willingness to experiment and a bit of patience as we master these tools together. Just $45, including the cost of materials!

Ely For Ely: Community Legacy & Transfer of Wealth
events.description: A significant amount of wealth is expected to transfer to Ely over the next 10-20 years, creating opportunities for community endowments, charitable giving, and legacy investments. This series of Ely for Ely gatherings will explore the scale of opportunity Ely has to embrace its huge reach to create lasting wealth for future generations. Together, we will learn more about estate planning, charitable tools, local giving pathways, and more. These meetings are open to all. Boundary Waters Connect facilitates an Ely for Ely planning committee, made up of local nonprofit leaders, business owners, and community members, to host a monthly networking and professional development program for Ely-area entrepreneurs, nonprofit leaders, and community members interested in making positive contributions to local affairs. The first meeting in each series will frame the conversation; the second will be an in-depth look at the track, maximizing Extension research, insights, and data. The third gathering will consider local applications and strategies for the future.

events.description: Have you ever looked at a broken piece of plastic, had a missing part for a project, or had a creative idea in your head and wished you could simply print the solution? “Introduction to 3D Modeling and Printing: From Idea to Object” with Tim Lutgen is the perfect place to turn those digital concepts into physical reality! Slated for three afternoons in a row, from 4 to 6 p.m. on Oct. 19-21, at Hurley High School, this course is designed for adults who are curious about the “how-to” behind 3D printing. Tim will demystify the process by breaking it down into two core components: designing, using CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software, and printing, learning how to “slice” your model and operate a 3D printer to bring it to life. No prior engineering experience is needed, just a willingness to experiment and a bit of patience as we master these tools together. Just $45, including the cost of materials!

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.title: The Fellow Travelers + Ross Thorn + Death Valley Yacht Club
events.venue: Cedar Lounge Earth Rider Brewery taproom
events.description: There’s a type of band that doesn’t just play songs — they collect them, test-drive them, stretch them, condense them, and send them back out however they’re meant to be. Fellow Travelers belong in that category. At the heart of it all is Max Niemann: armed with a six-string guitar, a harmonica rack, and a catalog of songs that feel lived-in – whether it’s a front porch blues or a sprawling piece of electric alchemy. With a pastoral upbringing in northern Wisconsin, Ross Thorn’s music emanates as a warm and soulful hymn, waking up optimistically beside a snow-covered window. His sharply crafted and often humorous lyrics—distinctly reminiscent of great folk artists like John Prine—reveal internal struggles of empathy, questions of human character and virtue, and a search for hope, often finding solace in some unanticipated truth. Based out of Duluth, Minnesota, Death Valley Yacht Club is the creative collaboration of musicians Charlie Jacobs and Alex Oberton. The two-piece band’s signature sound features their intricate vocal harmonies sung over the interplay between their tightly-arranged acoustic guitars.

events.description: Plan an adventure at the Iron County Historical Society Museum. Built in 1893 as the town hall for the now-vanished Town of Vaughn, the museum building was sold the following April to serve as the courthouse of Iron County. events.title: History Happy Hour
events.description: Step into the 1920s for an evening of cocktails, hors d’oeuvres, music, and history at Glensheen! Begin your evening by entering through the Juliet Balcony, where you’ll be greeted with a cocktail and hors d’oeuvres before heading downstairs to explore Glensheen’s basement. Discover 1920s-inspired activities and artifacts on display, enjoy music from the era, snap a photo in the billiards room, and take in a few surprises along the way. Enjoy a selection of fun, 1920s-inspired cocktails available for purchase at the cash bar before settling in for an engaging history talk by local historian Tony Dierckins. Tony will present “Drying Out Duluth: From Temperance to Prohibition,” exploring Duluth’s complicated relationship with alcohol—from the city’s early liquor ordinances and temperance movement to Prohibition and the creative ways Duluthians continued to enjoy a drink. Following the talk, enjoy dessert and a special 1920s-themed experience to round out the evening. Dress to impress and embrace the spirit of the 1920s for this one-of-a-kind night at Glensheen. This event is for guests ages 21 and older. Doors open at 5:30 p.m. | Talk begins at 6:30 p.m. | Event ends at 9 p.m.

events.title: The Root Beer Lady | Dorothy Molter Play
events.description: The Root Beer Lady | Dorothy Molter Play Thursday, October 22, 7:00 p.m. Arrowhead Center for the Arts, Grand Marais Friends of the Boundary waters presents a touring production of The Root Beer Lady . Written and presented by Kim Schultz, The Root Beer Lady tells the story of the indomitable Dorothy Molter, the last legal non-indigenous resident of the Boundary Waters. The story reflects the beauty and hardships of Molter’s solitary yet satisfying life beginning in 1934. The play, funny and passionate, explores her independence, fortitude, and love of nature. Molter pushes back against the premise that her time in the North Woods made her the “Loneliest Woman in America,” as the Saturday Evening Post claimed in 1952. Kim Schultz is a nationally and internationally acclaimed writer, actor, and solo show artist working across mediums. This marks Kim’s third solo show. The tour is produced by Bourgoin Productions.

events.title: Silent Film: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
events.description: The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. Perfect for the Halloween season, “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is spooky, stylish and historically significant. It is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. It is widely considered the first true horror story put to film. This masterpiece influenced later film directors such as Alfred Hitchcock and Tim Burton. Attendees are encouraged to come dressed for Halloween, adding to the film’s haunted atmosphere. Aaron David Miller returns to Sacred Heart Music Center to accompany this film on the Center’s outstanding Felgemaker pipe organ. Miller is noted for his highly imaginative and creative style, found in his performances, improvisations and compositions. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country.

events.title: The Northland Beckons: Writing in Haiku - Mount Royal Branch Library, Duluth
events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free writing workshops at participating ALS libraries from October 9-30, 2026. These workshops, presented by author Sandra Hisakuni, are titled: The Northland Beckons: Writing in Haiku . Grow your creativity and writing skills in this fun haiku workshop. Writers will learn the structure and form of haiku, its origins in Japanese literature, and how Sandra Hisakuni connects this writing practice to Minnesota's Northwoods. Workshop attendees will explore this powerful tool for mindfulness, joyful reflection, and playful expression. Writers will use words and art to create their own haiku masterpiece to take home. This program is 1 hour long and suited for adults, teens, and children ages 10 and up. These free programs are being offered at the following locations: Friday, October 9, 3:30 p.m. - Buhl Public Library Tuesday, October 13, 3:30 p.m. - International Falls Public Library Wednesday, October 14, 1:00 p.m. - Babbitt Public Library Thursday, October 15, 10:00 a.m. - Chisholm Public Library Thursday, October 15, 3:30 p.m. - Hibbing Public Library Friday, October 16, 1:00 p.m.

events.description: Cuban food and Live music with songwriter Shane Nelson Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

And just when you think it can’t get any better - the balloon drop brings the ultimate celebratory twist! Round up your crew, grab your tickets, and curate your most epic 90s ensemble. Babie Eyes also includes the synthesizer work of Kenny Bressler.

events.description: Spooktacular Silent Cinema: The Monster (1925) Date: Saturday, October 24th Time: 7:00 PM Tickets: $20 Step back into the golden age of horror-comedy with a special screening of the 1925 silent classic, The Monster! Directed by Roland West and starring horror legend Lon Chaney, this spine-tingling flick follows meek clerk and aspiring sleuth Johnny Goodlittle. Eager to solve a rash of mysterious highway abductions and win the heart of the lovely Betty, Johnny tracks sinister clues to a spooky, isolated asylum. There, he and his companions fall into the trap of the unhinged Dr. Ziska (Chaney), who has far more in store for them than a simple tour. Lock the doors and prepare for bizarre experiments, strange servants, and plenty of classic chilling thrills. Featuring Live Musical Accompaniment Enhance your experience with a live performance on our historic Barton Organ, performed by in-house composer and accompanist Tim Mesun. Tim will bring every jump-scare, shadow, and comedic twist to life in real-time, delivering an authentic 1920s moviegoing experience you won’t want to miss. Get your tickets today for an unforgettable night of classic horror, humor, and live music!

events.venue: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center
events.description: Ghosts in the Bong Center Museum Galleries! This Halloween season, the Bong Veterans Museum invites you to experience our museum in a whole new light. On October 24th, you can alter your vision and get spooky if you choose. The galleries will take on a mysterious atmosphere; visitors of all ages are welcome to wander through exhibits where history and imagination blur. Our mannequins have always stood watch, but during this special event you may find yourself asking—are they moving, or is it just the season playing tricks on you?Families can enjoy a mild, sensory-friendly adventure designed to spark curiosity without ever overwhelming younger visitors. For those who prefer a gentler experience, accommodations will be made to ensure everyone can participate at their own comfort level.This isn’t a haunted house—it’s a chance to celebrate the spooky season in a unique, educational, and welcoming environment. Discover the secrets of our mannequins, share in the fun of Halloween with your loved ones, and see the Bong Center like you’ve never seen it before. Regular admission applies.

events.description: The old Sportsmans Bar off of Normana RD, came hang out for great pizzas, and a live performance from songwriter Shane Nelson in a cozy small town vibe atmosphere. Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.title: Max Subar
events.description: Max Subar and Minor Moon Fall Duo Tour. DM for address Chicago singer-songwriter Max Subar joins the Merge Records roster with his debut full-length album "Anything Could Be." Laid down on a mobile recording rig in a house on the shore of a frozen lake in Wisconsin, Max emerged after ten days of solitude with a record of neither fallow nor verdant earth, but, staggeringly, one that occupies the threshold between the two, a space that accommodates the potential for stagnation and growth: their hopes, their worries, the time it takes to arrive at an unknown destination, and the courage to accept what’s there, waiting to be realized. “There is so much room for newness in the weightiest or seemingly most paralyzing of times,” Subar explains. “No matter how foreign, frightening, anxiety-ridden, or unfamiliar chapters of life can feel, there is always an opportunity to tap deep into ourselves and land somewhere new, somewhere forward.”

events.title: Minor Moon
events.description: house show, dm for address :: https://www.instagram.com/inclinestares/ Max Subar (duo) Minor Moon (duo) Kara Warren Minor Moon, The Light Up Waltz Out via Ruination Record Co., April 12th, 2024 At the heart of Minor Moon’s open-ended and knotty country rock songs is an undeniably inviting lightness. While the Chicago-based songwriter and bandleader Sam Cantor writes impressionistic songs about the end of the world, they’re wrapped in such a warm blanket of lush guitars and pastoral twang that they always leave a hopeful spark. On their latest LP, The Light Up Waltz, Cantor sings of the fantastical in magical traveling bands, swaying bridges, and aquamarine metamorphoses. Still, he’s concerned with fundamentally human questions about who we are and how we reinvent ourselves when everything crumbles around us. While the 2021 release of Minor Moon’s third LP Tethers coincided with a transitional period in Cantor’s life, The Light Up Waltz materialized during a time of unprecedented personal stability and creativity. He immersed himself in Chicago’s immensely collaborative music community performing live with V.V. Lightbody, Andrew Sa, Half Gringa, and more.

events.description: Is Autism an identity or a disorder, is an ongoing question which faces those who describe themselves under the umbrella of Neurodiversity language. WW Norton author, and autistic individual, Sean Inderbitzen LCSW, DSW, invites neurodiverse Duluthians to wrestle with this question with him in a small gathering setting. Themes to be covered from his new book in this talk include identity, temperment, disorder, empathy, and the role of ambiguous loss in shaping connection and rigidity. These themes like these and more appear in his new book Neural Exercises for Autism, and we invite you to meet with the author partaking in discussion, pastries, and a dive into meaning and neurodiversity. Please register for our gathering complete with readings, discussion, pastries from Sara’s Table at Chester Creek Cafe, and Alcoholic beverages available for purchase. events.title: Zach Williams
events.description: Music is meant to feel “lived-in,” not unlike a favorite old jacket or a first car. At least that’s what multiplatinum two-time GRAMMY® Award-winning Arkansas-born and Nashville-based maverick Zach Williams would say. Through a fusion of southern rock spirit and country soul, Zach creates music with an exterior which is worn down in the best way, but all heart underneath rough guitar riffs and gravelly vocals. You’ll not only hear his journey in the music, but you’ll also see it in his unfiltered storytelling—how he went from a tiny town to international stardom, selling out shows, toppling charts, and collaborating with the likes of Dolly Parton. Along the way, he battled addiction, anxiety, and insecurity, coming out on the other side with a whole lot to say. After living through the lowest of lows and the highest of highs, he made a choice to trust his gut more than ever in 2021. Doing so had certainly served him well up to this point, so he wholeheartedly embraced his most formative inspirations, including rock and old school country.

events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free writing workshops at participating ALS libraries from October 9-30, 2026. These workshops, presented by author Sandra Hisakuni, are titled: The Northland Beckons: Writing in Haiku . Grow your creativity and writing skills in this fun haiku workshop. Writers will learn the structure and form of haiku, its origins in Japanese literature, and how Sandra Hisakuni connects this writing practice to Minnesota's Northwoods. Workshop attendees will explore this powerful tool for mindfulness, joyful reflection, and playful expression. Writers will use words and art to create their own haiku masterpiece to take home. This program is 1 hour long and suited for adults, teens, and children ages 10 and up. events.description: Oh yeah, we have a Halloween bash here. And we're bringing the place down as the headlining act. There still lots of info TBA as this show gets put together. What we know: 1 hour set from yours truly from 9pm-10pm. Costumes. And Modern Day Wasteland will also be there, plus a couple other bands TBD. We'll update this event as soon as we know more! But for now, you know when and where! Formed in January 2014 and having a few facelifts since then, Mad Alice is still delivering the mighty music of Alice in Chains and Mad Season to anyone that would hear it. Huge fans of both bands, Mad Alice tries to deliver a show packed with accurate performances of the songs as are on the albums. This means two guitar players, this means many vocal harmonies. Covering material spanning the early demos to Music Bank, Mad Alice could be considered a tribute to Layne Staley. Attendees at a Mad Alice show can expect to hear a set half loaded with hit singles, with the other half reaching a little deeper into the AIC & MS catalog. And the set changes from show to show to keep things fresh. Come one, come all... and let's celebrate some great music from a fantastic time!

events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: DECONSTRUCTING THE MUSIC LIVE! THE DARK SIDE OF THE MOON A Multimedia Presentation Hosted by Public Television Host SCOTT FREIMAN “Scott’s talk was fascinating! I learned stuff I never knew before – and I was there!” Peter Asher, Grammy-Winning Producer/Artist/Manager and Sirius XM Radio Host In Deconstructing The Music LIVE: Pink Floyd’s The Dark Side of the Moon, Scott Freiman, host of the Public Television series Deconstructing the Beatles, celebrates Pink Floyd’s groundbreaking 1973 album with his first non-Beatles “deconstruction.” Scott will take you on a track-by-track journey through this Pink Floyd masterpiece, explaining the inspiration for the songs and their evolution in the studio. Dark Side of the Moon is a concept album that explores themes of life, death, time, and the human experience. The album features nine tracks that seamlessly flow into each other, creating a cohesive and immersive listening experience. Musically, the album pushed the boundaries of rock music, incorporating elements of jazz, classical, and experimental music.

events.description: Admission $12.00 Location NLDC Lodge or Amphitheater Description Wherever you are in your yoga practice, this class is for you. Lakeside Yoga is a gently paced class that encourages deep release in the body's major muscle groups. Lakeside Yoga also helps build strength and cultivates balance in both body and mind. Whether you're new to yoga or a seasoned practitioner, you'll leave feeling grounded, refreshed, and restored. events.title: Iron County Historical Museum
events.description: Plan an adventure at the Iron County Historical Society Museum. Built in 1893 as the town hall for the now-vanished Town of Vaughn, the museum building was sold the following April to serve as the courthouse of Iron County. The Museum offers you three full floors of display from history of iron mining to railroads, timber to veterans, home life to faith based articles. The museum is filled with many old photos showing life in the past. May thru October MON/WED/FRI/SAT 1OAM-2PM, NOVEMBER - APRIL WED/FRI/SAT.

events.title: Duluth Haunted Ship 2026
events.description: Welcome to the home of the William A. Irvin Haunted Ship Tours in Duluth, Minnesota! That hint of cool breeze you feel isn’t just a change of weather. Those are the spirits of the Duluth Haunted Ship swinging on anchor just outside your view. The ghouls on board are waiting to morph the William A. Irvin historic freighter into something truly sinister. This season marks the 31st year of this unhallowed event, starting Friday, October 2, 2026 and running long weekends through Halloween (plus MEA Wednesday, October 14, 2026). This year, you can look forward to more activity outside of the ship on Harbor Drive: enjoy food trucks every Friday & Saturday, lights, bonfires, drinks available for purchase, and more. Avoid the General Admission (GA) line and buy a FAST PASS ticket. Enter through FAST PASS gate. General Admission tickets enter through the GA line. All tickets are valid for one tour. You may arrive anytime during open hours for the date that your ticket is valid. Tickets can be purchased at the gate. No child under the age of 12 will be admitted without a caregiver. The ship is not handicapped accessible. All sales are final. No refunds.

events.description: Duluth's biggest costume party. Halloween night at Clyde Iron Works with Weska and Techno Club. Truesoul, Drumcode, Experts Only, REALM, Armada, HYPERWAX Weska doesn’t just make tracks — he builds worlds. Toronto-born and globally seasoned, Weska is a versatile creator and performer who’s carved out a space between groove-driven techno, heavy-hitting progressive house, and the melodic textures of indie dance. His sound is immersive yet direct, designed for big moments, built on nuance. It's this distinctive approach that’s earned him the respect of major players like Adam Beyer, John Summit, and Gorgon City. After early breakthroughs on labels like Drumcode, Cocoon, and Bedrock, Weska’s rise has only accelerated. More recently, he's showcased his forward-thinking sound on platforms like Experts Only, Realm, and Armada, proving his versatility without compromising his identity. A fast-rising tastemaker with a natural instinct for momentum, Weska has taken his sound across continents.

events.title: Nu-Blu Bluegrass Artists
events.description: Nu-Blu, based in Siler City in central North Carolina, is comprised of Carolyn Routh, who handles bass and vocals; Austin Hefflefinger on vocals and banjo; Justin Harrison, on mandolin and fiddle; and Daniel Routh, who is the band’s Renaissance Man – guitarist, singer, manager, and tour coordinator, among many other roles. The group brings its lively and entertaining version of Americana-bluegrass music to audiences across the nation year-round. Their sound acknowledges the traditional institutions that have shaped it, yet is innovative and daring enough to bring a fresh sparkle to contemporary acoustic music that lands them squarely in the forefront of bands blazing the trail in acoustic entertainment. Influences range from the sounds of original bluegrass pioneers like Earl Scruggs, Jimmy Martin and Lester Flatt to rock bands of the 1980’s, and modern contemporary sounds such as Alison Krauss and Union Station. Carolyn’s soprano vocal approach might be described as similar to Ms. Krauss, except she carries a phrasing and emotional elegance that shows a clear originality.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

Jason takes classic songs and flips them with his own twist — smooth grooves, sharp turns, and those little “wait... run that back” moments that catch the whole room at once. Bring your crew, grab a drink, and let Wednesday night get a little indecent. come out and get Indecent 😈😎🎸🤘💜 www.indyp218.com Indecent Proposal is a band out of Duluth, Minnesota, built around connection, feel, and songs that hold up in a room full of people. Blending modern alt-rock, groove-driven covers, and emotionally grounded originals, the band focuses on moments you can feel as much as hear. Their live shows move fluidly between intimacy and release—quiet verses, loud hearts, and choruses that come back at you from the crowd. Led by frontman Josh Brown, with Selie’s dynamic vocals, Jason Soderlund on guitar, Terry Beckman on bass, and Andy Fabian on drums, Indecent Proposal brings intention to every set and honesty to every song.

events.title: Ian Alexy
events.description: Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life. “Invokes 80s era Petty and Springsteen.” - Minneapolis Star Tribune “Stomping Blues Rock reminiscent of Dan Auerbach.”

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.description: Andreas Klein is widely admired as a pianist of rare sensitivity and musicality. The Washington Post has praised his “articulate and flowing pianism” while the New York Times called him “a pianist who makes silences sound like music.” About a recent Glenn Gould tribute (with the Minguet String Quartet), the Calgary Herald reported, “(Klein brings) to his performance a mature understanding...as well as a brilliant execution”, while Classical Voice of North Carolina (CVNC) was even more blunt: “Andreas Klein is a stupendous pianist...a stunning performance by any standard, and it brought the audience to its feet in a rousing ovation.” He has performed in many of the leading houses of Europe, from Wigmore Hall in London to the Berlin Philharmonie, as well as Carnegie Hall in New York and the Kennedy Center in Washington DC, and is at home with the grandeur of playing with the Berlin Philharmonic or the vast reaches of the Ravinia Festival (where he received two standing ovations) as he is with the intimacy of Le Poisson Rouge (NYC).

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.title: Teague Alexy
events.description: Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs. Teague’s first album of 2017, Circuit Sessions, combines multiple musical genres into a powerful new collection of Teague’s poetic songs with the lionstrong production and rhythm section of Eric Pollard (Actual Wolf) and Steve Garrington (Low) joined by Minneapolis guitarist Jake Hanson. Teague also has a new musical and storytelling podcast “Wisecracks & Roadside Flats.”

events.description: Tickets on sale now! #IMOMSOHARD The Crashing Out Tour: Two moms, lots of laughs —creators of the popular web series and podcast on tour This is an age 18+ show. Saturday, November 7 | DECC Symphony Hall | 8:00pm Tickets on sale now! #IMOMSOHARD began as a popular web series by real-life best friends, comedians, and moms, Kristin Hensley and Jen Smedley. One night, over a glass of wine and many tears of frustration, these two friends decided to tell a different kind of story. With a camera, two husbands, a babysitter, and bottomless mimosas, Kristin and Jen decided to speak openly about their fears and failures and to prove that the only way to survive motherhood is through laughter and friendship. The video was a smash hit, sparking an online community of two million of the most engaged followers – confirmation that moms and women everywhere need to laugh and be heard.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.title: Styx
events.description: The six men comprising STYX have committed to rocking the Paradise together with audiences far and wide by averaging over 100 shows a year every year since (yes) 1999, and each one of them is committed to making the next show better than the last. Founded in Chicago in 1972, STYX has the unique distinction of being the first band in rock history to have four consecutive certified multimillion-selling albums in a row: 1977’s The Grand Illusion, 1978’s Pieces of Eight, 1979’s Cornerstone, and 1981’s Paradise Theatre. STYX draws from over four decades of barnburning chart hits, joyous singalongs, and harddriving deep cuts. Like a symphony that builds to a satisfying crescendo, a STYX set covers a wide range of stylistic cornerstones.

events.title: Amy Speace
events.description: A tour celebrating the launch of Amy's debut book of poetry, "The Cardinals" (Red Hen Press). She will be singing and reading selections from the book, which will be on sale at the show. Heralded by Rolling Stone, Billboard Magazine and The New York Times and featured on NPR’s “All Things Considered”, Amy Speace was discovered by Judy Collins, who signed her to her record label and has recorded her songs. She’s the 2020 winner of the AMA UK’s International Song of the Year. Her newest record, “The American Dream,” was released October 18th and became the #1 record and the title track was named #1 song in the FAI Radio Charts for its first month out. Her song, “The Weight of the World” was named the #4 record of last decade by WFUV, NYC. As well, her song, “The Sea and the Shore” was named as one of the 100 best folk songs of the era. She will be releasing a single of Woody Guthrie’s “Plane Wreck at Los Gatos” this summer accompanied by a video, to help raise awareness for the ACLU. A writer’s writer, her forthcoming debut collection of poetry will be published by Red Hen Press in Spring 2027.

events.title: Them Coulee Boys
events.description: “A rollicking blend of bluegrass, folk, and rock and roll” - Folk Alley Soren Staff and Beau Janke—co-founders of folk/rock/Americana outfit Them Coulee Boys—met as camp counselors in northern Wisconsin in 2011. Their weekend workshopping of Avett Brothers and classic country tunes led to original songs and adding Soren’s brother Jens on mandolin, Neil Krause on electric bass and Stas Hable on drums. The band’s name is a nod to the glacial melt-carved river valleys they call home, known by early French fur trappers as coulees. Known for wild swings of emotion during sets, it is not unusual to see fans in tears and minutes later dancing with abandon. The honesty and ability to talk and sing about the feelings and emotions that shape them has endeared them to a growing group of fans and friends. Over the course of five albums, the band has garnered international attention and earned press in Americana UK, American Songwriter, Ditty TV, Folk Alley, and The Bluegrass Situation.

events.title: #IMOMSOHARD

And a tour bus (you didn’t think they’d leave them with their husbands, did you?). There’s no one making moms feel as uncomfortably normal as Kristin Hensley and Jen Smedley, the hilarious oh-so-real women behind #IMomSoHard. With over 675,000 Facebook fans, and more than 55 million views of their web series, Jen and Kristin’s blend of honesty and humor offer the kinds of levity most of us only get from our therapist, proving that if we weren’t all laughing, we’d be crying, right? Right!? Sure to deliver the kind of straight talk you can only get from discussing body hair in the kids’ playroom while sipping mimosas, Kristin and Jen prove you can’t make this shi*t up. It’s like an evening with two of your besties. But funnier. And probably with more drinking.

events.description: No Hard Feelings Tour Tickets on Sale Now! ABOUT GARY OWEN Gary Owen has been entertaining audiences for more than two decades with his sharp observational humor and fearless storytelling. Known for his unapologetic, rule-defying style, his material draws from his personal life, time in the military and the everyday absurdities that connect people across backgrounds. With a fanbase that has grown by the millions in recent months and continues to surge across social media, Owen’s reach has cemented his place as one of the most in-demand touring comedians today. Beyond stand-up, Owen has appeared in a wide range of feature films including BACK ON THE STRIP with Tiffany Haddish and Wesley Snipes, MEET THE BLACKS and its sequel THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR, THINK LIKE A MAN and THINK LIKE A MAN TOO, RIDE ALONG with Ice Cube and Kevin Hart, LITTLE MAN opposite the Wayans Brothers, and DADDY DAY CARE with Eddie Murphy. He is also widely recognized for his scene-stealing role as “Bearcat” in the MGM film COLLEGE. On television, Owen starred in his own BET series THE GARY OWEN SHOW and co-hosted TruTV’s sketch series UPLOAD WITH SHAQUILLE O’NEAL.

events.title: An Evening With Neil deGrasse Tyson
events.description: An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I Presented by Roberts Group Tickets on sale now! “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security.

events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. events.title: Leonids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Leonids meteor shower offers clear-sky meteor rates of about 10 to 15 shooting stars per hour. They are active between Nov. 6 - 30 and will peak on Nov. 17-18. The Leonids are bright meteors and have a high percentage of persistent trains according to AMS. The Leonids' radiant is located in the sickle-shaped head of the constellation Leo, the lion. Leonid meteor hunting can be incredible, or a total bust. It all depends on where its parent body, Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, will be in its orbit and the kind of debris clumps that will be around when our planet passes through this comet's orbit.

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society.

events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. events.title: DECC Gala: a Progressive Party Through the Decades
events.description: The First-Ever DECC Gala: a Progressive Party through the Decades We're excited to announce the inaugural DECC Gala, a one-of-a-kind celebration honoring the 60th Anniversary of the DECC. This isn't your typical gala because the DECC, with 10 community venues, is anything but typical. Guests will embark on a progressive journey through the decades and across the DECC campus, experiencing the history of the organization in a truly immersive way. The evening begins in Symphony Hall, celebrating the 1960s with food, beverages, and entertainment inspired by the decade in which the DECC was founded. From there, guests will move throughout the campus, with each venue representing a different era, complete with themed food, drinks, and experiences. The celebration culminates in AMSOIL Arena, where we'll arrive in the 2020s and toast to the future of the DECC. Join us for an unforgettable evening celebrating six decades of memories, milestones, and community impact.

events.title: Barron Ryan
events.venue: Rock Ridge High School Performing Arts Center
events.description: Barron Ryan’s love for music has always been divided. The son of two musicians, he grew up in a house filled with the sounds of everything ranging from Beethoven to James Brown. So when it comes to his own performing, he’s not content drawing on just one of those influences; he combines them all into an adventure that’s vintage yet fresh, historical yet hip, classic yet cool. Even when beginning to make his own music, Barron needed more than one outlet. He started piano lessons at the age of four, but at the same time began teaching himself drums. While progressing through middle and high schools, he won prizes in classical piano competitions while also earning a reputation as a formidable jazz drummer. In college, Barron continued to excel in multiple fields, majoring in piano performance and even earning a spot playing snare in the marching band drumline. Though he increasingly turned his focus toward the piano, the genres of classical, jazz, and funk continued to attract his attention. Now Barron applies his myriad interests and expertise to create an awe-inspiring program.

events.description: Ian Alexy plays solo acoustic (with looping and effects, of course) on the third Saturday of every month at Sir Benedict's in Duluth. Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life.

events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.description: 1st of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. While the Frost Moon and Freezing Moon are self-explanatory, November's full moon is most known as the Beaver Moon. Beavers are quite active preparing for winter. Also known as the Mourning Moon, due to the increase in darkness.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings (nee Turany) and has a son, August, born in January 2003. Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally. His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock. 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life.

events.description: Live music with songwriter Shane Nelson -grab some authentic Cubin food, a drink and a seat, and enjoy an evening of listening. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Shane Nelson - Havanas
events.description: Cuban food and songwriting, From Shane Nelson Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.description: The Event Center, Floodwood GB Leighton acoustic show The Event Center, Floodwood 201 West 7th Avenue Floodwood, MN 55736 More than 200 shows a year. Jubilant fans who follow him from Minnesota to Mexico. More than 100,000 albums sold. A new release “Get Up” and a state-of-the-art nightclub named after one of his songs -- all without the support of a major record label... Meet GB Leighton, a band named after one of the regions’ most incendiary live performers and consistently solid songwriters, Brian Leighton. Through more than a decade and eleven studio albums, Leighton and his five piece band have been tearing up rock clubs, festivals and even a few fan’s living rooms with a slew of songs that connect with the heart and couples singing along out on the dance floor. “A man of the people” is a phrase usually reserved for statesmen and politicians, but for Leighton, it’s a fitting description when you see him in action working a crowd. events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | Ursa Minor Brewing
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music along with a few covers. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The Snowman is back at the Reif with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra for a second December, on its way to becoming a Grand Rapids tradition. The 1982 animated film, based on Raymond Briggs’ picture book, has no dialogue. A boy builds a snowman, the snowman comes to life, and together they fly off into the night sky to “Walking in the Air.” Howard Blake’s music tells the whole story, and the Itasca Symphony Orchestra plays it live while the film fills the big screen. The rest of the afternoon is holiday music for the whole family. Bring the kids and the grandparents, and make it part of your December.

events.title: Ian Alexy: Every Third Saturday at Sir Ben's
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Ian Alexy plays solo acoustic (with looping and effects, of course) on the third Saturday of every month at Sir Benedict's in Duluth. Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz & Jimmy Rogers | Sir Bens Tavern
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.title: December Full Moon

events.description: 2nd of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. December's full moon is known as the Cold Moon or Long Nights Moon. In addition to the shortest daylight day of the year, the Long Nights Moon pertains to the amount of time the moon is above the horizon. It takes a high trajectory across the sky because it is opposite to the low sun.

events.title: Andrew Crowley: Lyon's Pub 8pm
events.description: Andrew Crowley on the piano Andrew Crowley is a Twin Cities-based musician, composer, and audio engineer with a dynamic career spanning from major label rock stages to the baseball diamond. A certified Hammond Organ artist who studied through the Berklee School of Music, Andrew can often be found during the summer serving as the Musical Director and ballpark organist for the Saint Paul Saints, delivering live musical energy and stadium-sized sound at CHS Field. He can also be found leading a packed house in piano sing-alongs at Lyon's Pub, composing music for films, documentaries, and commercials, or working behind the console. He became internationally known in the 1990s as the frontman for Columbia Records' Fat Tuesday. Since then, a life of live performance has led to some pretty great happy accidents—like winding up on the outtakes of Pearl Jam’s 2003 Live at the Garden release, singing with Iggy Pop, playing with blues legends like Elvin Bishop, and many other things. Today, whether he is at the ballpark, the concert stage, or the pub, Andrew's career is built on a relentless passion for authentic, high-quality music.

events.description: 3rd of 3 supermoons A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. The January full moon is most often known as the Wolf Moon because it is the month hungry wolves howl in the night. It is also known as the Stay Home, or Quiet, Moon as cold temps set in and we want to snuggle in and stay home.
